correctness.rationale: The pair-column state construction is bijective with labelled proper conflict-free prism colourings. Its 18- and 84-state transition characteristic polynomials are checked in full by an independent standard-library Newton-identity implementation using exact integer matrix traces; the formal log-determinant trace identity proves the universal generating functions. All 6,498,957 tested full assignment words match independent direct edge/neighbourhood enumeration for q=3, n=3..7 and q=4, n=3..5. Constructive closed walks of lengths 3,4,5 sharing one state establish four-colour existence for every n>=3, while a three-colour trace factor gives the exact 3-divisibility obstruction. Rouché bounds and elementary root signs justify the asymptotic rate; the ordinary prism transfer has leading eigenvalue 7. The proof excludes n<3 and palettes other than q=3,4.

The stronger list-colouring guarantee addresses colour availability rather than the number of admitted labelled assignments. None of the inspected published results has stronger numerical coverage of the present exact census.

originality.rationale: The claim is the all-length exact named-colouring count for proper conflict-free three- and four-colourings of prisms, including the degree-36 spectral determinant, optimal-colouring multiplicities, and conditional exponential rate. The 2023 prism result gives existence ranges for uniformly two-homogeneous colourings, not these counts. The 2026 prism chromatic-polynomial analysis counts all proper colourings and does not enforce neighbourhood uniqueness. The recent proper conflict-free list-colouring papers concern existence under sparseness hypotheses rather than enumeration on cubic prisms. Explicit semantic and database comparisons below found no statement implying this exact enumeration; historical-priority uncertainty remains.

value.rationale: The exact number of optimal palette colourings is a natural finer invariant than chromatic number for a fixed common graph family. The established prism theorem determines the minimum palette but does not count admissible assignments; the 84-state neighbourhood transfer yields a nontrivial seven-factor determinant, exact infinite counting sequence, and quantitative decay of the fraction of ordinary proper four-colourings meeting the local uniqueness requirement. These precise statistics compare constrained and unconstrained colourings, not arbitrary slices or minor numeric gains.
